title: Germany looks to finalize a new trade deal with the U.S. before the end of summer
body: Chancellor Friedrich Merz has said Germany is pushing to finalize a new trade agreement with the U.S. before the end of summer. Merz acknowledged that a resolution could significantly relieve industrial and equity markets sensitive to trade developments. Several countries are locked in negotiations with U.S. President Donald Trump to clinch some trade deals before the U.S. issues stringent reciprocal tariffs, which are threatened for next month. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent also said the date could be pushed back later for nations thought to be negotiating in good faith. Germany’s Merz expects auto tariffs, steel, and aluminum tariffs in negotiations GERMANY EXPECTS US TARIFF DEAL BY SUMMER – MERZ Chancellor Merz told ARD he expects a resolution to the US-EU tariff dispute before summer ends. This signals progress in trade diplomacy and may ease tension on autos and industrials, offering relief to equity markets sensitive to… pic.twitter.com/ezyU2tTS9J — Naeem Aslam (@NaeemAslam23) June 17, 2025 The current U.S. tariff pause is set to expire in early July, adding pressure for both sides to reach terms swiftly. Merz argued that even if that deadline is missed, a full agreement may still be wrapped up by late summer. World leaders assembled at this week’s Group of Seven summit in Canada to push U.S. President Donald Trump to back away from his trade war, which has caused tensions in global economic stability. Most nations represented at the G7 are already subject to Trump’s 10% baseline tariff, with threats of more to come. Merz stated that key areas of the agreement are expected to include auto tariffs, steel and aluminum duties, and a potential “zero-for-zero” tariff swap. He also told reporters at the summit on Sunday that he would team up with his counterparts from France and Italy to directly discuss the U.S. trade threat with Trump. “Emmanuel Macron [French President], Giorgia Meloni [Italian Prime Minister], and I are firmly resolved to try, over the next two days, to talk again with the U.S. government to see if we can find a solution.” -Fredrich Merz, German Chancellor. Last month, German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil called for serious negotiations with the U.S. after Trump threatened to impose 50 percent tariffs on European Union goods starting June 1. He also believes that the levies endanger the American economy at least as much as the German and European economies. Klingbeil also mentioned earlier this month that the new government in Berlin is seeking to pass a 46B euro package of corporate tax breaks over the summer. The announcement came on the day that Trump’s new levies on steel and aluminum came into effect. Trump says EU not offering fair trade deal, Japan being ‘tough’ too Trump left the G7 after finalizing a trade deal with the United Kingdom. He highlighted roadblocks on other fronts, saying Tuesday that Japan was being “tough” in trade talks and the European Union failed to offer a fair deal. After leaving the summit early to return to Washington, the President said he was in talks with the EU but didn’t feel that they’re offering a fair deal yet. Trump also noted that the EU would either make a good deal or pay whatever the U.S. says they must. In a veiled plea for Trump to back off from his tariff onslaught, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen appealed to keep trade between them and the U.S. fair, predictable, and open. The President revealed that Japan would soon receive a letter he had threatened to send to U.S. trading partners who did not reach a deal. Trump called the Japanese tough but argued that in the end, they would get a letter saying, “This is what you’re going to pay.” He also mentioned that pharmaceutical tariffs will be coming very soon. At the summit, Trump and British Prime Minister Keir Starmer signed the trade deal agreed upon last month. He said the U.S.’s relationship with Britain was “just fantastic,” confirming that they signed the agreement and it’s done. Britain was the first country to sign a preliminary deal with Washington to avoid deeper tariffs, although the 10 percent baseline levy has remained in place. The U.S. President also mentioned on the first day of the G7 gathering that a trade deal with Canada was possible. He argued that both countries have different concepts, saying that he has a tariff concept and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has a different concept. title: BBVA Advises Wealthy Clients to Allocate Up to 7% in Bitcoin and Ether
body: BBVA's private banking division is now advising clients to allocate a portion of their investments to cryptocurrencies, depending on individual risk tolerance. Philippe Meyer, Head of Digital and Blockchain Solutions at BBVA Switzerland, announced this strategy at the DigiAssets conference in London. He noted that clients with higher risk appetites are being guided to invest up to 7% in digital assets. This move is notable as it reflects a growing acceptance of cryptocurrencies within mainstream finance. While many banks have been cautious, BBVA has been facilitating crypto purchases for clients since 2021. Meyer believes BBVA is among the first major global banks to actively recommend cryptocurrency investments to its clients. Despite ongoing regulatory warnings about the risks associated with cryptocurrencies, BBVA maintains that a modest exposure—starting at 3%—can enhance portfolio performance without significant risk. The bank's current recommendations focus on Bitcoin and Ether, with plans to include other cryptocurrencies later this year. This development comes amid a resurgence in cryptocurrency markets, with Bitcoin reaching new highs in May. The rebound follows a downturn in 2022, influenced by the collapse of major exchanges like FTX. Supportive policies, such as U.S. President Donald Trump's pro-crypto stance, have also contributed to renewed investor interest.

title: Decentralized AI: Gradient Network Secures $10M for Revolutionary AI Infrastructure
body: BitcoinWorld Decentralized AI: Gradient Network Secures $10M for Revolutionary AI Infrastructure In the rapidly evolving landscape where artificial intelligence meets blockchain technology, a significant development has captured the attention of innovators and investors alike. Gradient Network, a company dedicated to pushing the boundaries of AI, has just announced a substantial funding round, signaling a major step forward in the quest to build robust and privacy-preserving Decentralized AI solutions. What is Gradient Network and Why is Decentralized AI Important? Gradient Network is positioning itself at the forefront of developing AI systems that operate outside the traditional centralized models. Their core mission revolves around creating a decentralized infrastructure designed to enhance user privacy and improve access to artificial intelligence capabilities. This is a critical distinction in a world increasingly reliant on AI, where concerns about data ownership, censorship, and the concentration of power in the hands of a few tech giants are growing. Centralized AI models often require users to hand over vast amounts of data to a single entity, raising privacy red flags. They can also be susceptible to single points of failure or censorship. Decentralized AI aims to distribute the components of AI development, training, and deployment across a network, potentially offering: Enhanced Privacy: Data can be processed or models trained without raw information leaving the user’s control or being held by a single custodian. Increased Resilience: A decentralized network is less vulnerable to shutdowns or attacks than a single server or data center. Improved Access: By lowering the barriers to entry for both developers and users, decentralized systems can make AI tools more widely available. Greater Transparency: Using blockchain, certain aspects of AI model training or decision-making can potentially be made verifiable and transparent. Gradient Network’s focus on these areas highlights a clear vision for a more open, secure, and user-centric AI future. Securing Substantial Crypto Funding: Who is Investing? Gradient Network recently announced via its official blog that it has successfully raised $10 million in a seed funding round. This is a significant injection of capital for a company operating in the nascent decentralized AI space. The round was co-led by two prominent names in the blockchain and crypto investment world: Pantera Capital and Multicoin Capital. Participation also came from HSG and a consortium of other investors. The involvement of firms like Pantera Capital and Multicoin Capital is noteworthy. Both have a track record of identifying and investing in projects they believe will shape the future of decentralized technologies and digital assets. Their investment in Gradient Network suggests a strong belief in the company’s approach to Decentralized AI and the potential market for decentralized AI infrastructure. Securing this level of Crypto funding indicates several things: Investor confidence in Gradient Network’s team and technology roadmap. Recognition of the growing demand for privacy-preserving and decentralized AI solutions. Belief that the intersection of AI and blockchain represents a significant future market opportunity. The capital provides Gradient Network with the resources needed to accelerate development and scale their operations. Building the Future: What Does This Mean for AI Infrastructure? The $10 million raised is earmarked for building the core AI infrastructure that Gradient Network envisions. This infrastructure is not just about creating AI models; it’s about creating the underlying network and tools that enable decentralized AI applications to function effectively. Think of it as building the roads, power lines, and foundational utilities for a new type of AI ecosystem. Key components of this decentralized AI infrastructure likely include: Decentralized Compute Resources: Allowing users or organizations to contribute computing power for training or running AI models, potentially creating a marketplace for AI compute. Secure Data Handling: Mechanisms to process or train on data without compromising privacy, possibly using techniques like federated learning or homomorphic encryption in conjunction with decentralized storage. Model Training and Deployment Platforms: Tools that allow developers to build, train, and deploy AI models on the decentralized network. Incentive Mechanisms: Tokenomics or other systems to reward participants who contribute resources (compute, data, models) to the network. Developing such infrastructure is complex and capital-intensive. The funding round provides Gradient Network with the necessary resources to tackle these technical challenges and build a robust, scalable foundation for decentralized AI applications. Exploring the Potential of Blockchain AI While the announcement specifically mentions ‘decentralized AI’, the involvement of crypto-native investors like Pantera and Multicoin strongly suggests that blockchain technology plays a crucial role in Gradient Network’s plans. The term Blockchain AI refers to the integration of blockchain technology with artificial intelligence. How might Blockchain AI manifest within Gradient Network’s infrastructure? Blockchain Element Potential AI Integration Smart Contracts Automating agreements for AI model usage, data sharing, or compute resource allocation. Decentralized Ledgers Recording AI model provenance, training data sources, or audit trails for transparency and verifiability. Tokens Incentivizing network participants (compute providers, data owners, model developers) or facilitating payments for AI services. Decentralized Identity Securely managing access to AI models or data based on verifiable credentials. The combination of blockchain’s properties (immutability, transparency, decentralization) with AI’s capabilities could unlock new use cases and models for AI development and consumption that are not possible with traditional centralized approaches. Gradient Network is likely leveraging these synergies to build their unique offering. Beyond the Hype: Challenges and Opportunities for Gradient Network While the vision for Decentralized AI and Blockchain AI is compelling, the path forward is not without challenges. Gradient Network will need to navigate several hurdles to successfully build and scale its infrastructure: Technical Complexity: Building truly decentralized and performant AI infrastructure is incredibly difficult. It requires innovation in distributed systems, cryptography, and machine learning. Scalability: AI model training and inference are computationally intensive. Scaling a decentralized network to handle significant AI workloads efficiently is a major technical challenge. Adoption: Convincing developers and businesses to move away from established centralized AI platforms and adopt a new decentralized paradigm will require demonstrating clear advantages and ease of use. Regulatory Uncertainty: The intersection of AI, blockchain, and data privacy is a complex area with evolving regulations globally. Competition: While the decentralized AI space is young, other projects and companies are also exploring similar ideas. Despite these challenges, the opportunities are substantial. If Gradient Network can successfully deliver on its promise, it could tap into a massive market demand for privacy-preserving AI, create new economic models for AI development and usage, and contribute to a more open and equitable AI landscape. The $10 million in Crypto funding provides them with a strong starting point to tackle these challenges head-on. Actionable Insights and the Road Ahead For those interested in the future of AI and blockchain, Gradient Network’s development is worth watching. Here are some actionable insights: For Developers: Keep an eye on Gradient Network’s technical progress and potential SDKs or APIs. A decentralized AI infrastructure could offer new ways to build and deploy AI applications with enhanced privacy features. For Investors: While this seed round is closed, the project’s progress could signal future investment opportunities or the potential for a native token if their model involves one. Understand the technology and market need thoroughly. For Users: As decentralized AI infrastructure matures, look for applications built on platforms like Gradient Network that offer greater control over your data and transparent AI interactions. Stay Informed: Follow Gradient Network’s official channels and industry news to track their milestones and the broader developments in the decentralized AI and Blockchain AI space. The road ahead involves significant development work, community building, and demonstrating the tangible benefits of their approach compared to centralized alternatives. The successful Crypto funding round is a vote of confidence, but the real work of building the future of AI infrastructure lies ahead for Gradient Network . Conclusion Gradient Network’s successful $10 million seed funding round, backed by notable investors like Pantera Capital and Multicoin Capital, marks a pivotal moment for the development of Decentralized AI . By focusing on user privacy and improved access, the company is addressing critical limitations of current centralized AI models. The capital infusion provides the necessary resources to build the foundational AI infrastructure required for a decentralized ecosystem, potentially leveraging the unique capabilities of Blockchain AI . While challenges remain, the opportunity to create a more open, private, and resilient AI future is immense. As Gradient Network progresses, its journey will be a key indicator of the potential for decentralized technologies to reshape the field of artificial intelligence. title: Pump.fun’s quiet return to X offers no clarity, just crypto’s latest cautionary tale
body: Pump.fun’s reappearance on X is dramatic: sudden suspension, rampant theories, then a quiet return in less than 24 hours. No answers, just a more paranoid market left picking up the pieces. On June 16, without warning or explanation, the official X account for Pump.fun, the Solana-based memecoin launchpad, was abruptly taken offline. Shortly after, the personal handle of co-founder Alon Cohen (@a1lon9) also vanished. The unexpected purge didn’t stop there. Several other accounts tied to high-profile token platforms, including GMGN, Bloom Trading, and ElizaOS, were swept up in what appeared to many as a coordinated crackdown, raising more questions than answers. Was this X enforcing new policies? A shadowban by overzealous moderators? Or, more ominously, the first sign of regulatory pressure on Solana’s hyperactive memecoin ecosystem? Then, just as suddenly, the accounts were restored. X offered no justification for either decision, leaving traders to wonder whether the episode was a glitch, a warning, or pure bureaucratic randomness. You might also like: Why is Pi Network token down today? Keen users quickly noted Pump.fun’s unceremonious comeback on X and raised concerns about what might be happening behind the scenes. https://t.co/eZhMtacwIT is back and I'm left to wonder what's really going on in the crypto space are all the recent happenings mere coincidences or is there a back story somewhere? Well we keep our eyes primed for more updates, and hope to be on the winning team. https://t.co/pvjbEM7KM6 — Vindex Victor (@EjimV221) June 17, 2025 A billion-dollar memecoin moment under fire The social media blackout came just as Pump.fun was gearing up for a massive token offering, rumored to target a valuation near $1 billion. The reported plan drew both attention and backlash, as Pump.fun’s meteoric rise in 2024–25 made it a poster child for rapid-fire memecoin activity. Founded in January 2024 by Alon Cohen and his team, the platform has hosted more than six million token launches and generated over $350 million in annual revenue. But this growth hasn’t come without scrutiny. In November, Pump.fun was forced to disable its livestream feature after users exploited it to broadcast everything from violent threats to explicit content. That incident exposed the darker side of memecoin culture and how quickly unregulated platforms can spiral into chaos. Now, with its rumored $1 billion token sale drawing mainstream attention, regulators appear to be taking notice. While no agency has publicly claimed responsibility for the X suspensions, the U.S. SEC has been increasingly vocal about cracking down on what it sees as unregistered securities offerings, a category that could easily include memecoin launchpads. What makes this episode particularly troubling for crypto is how it exposes the industry’s dependence on platforms it doesn’t control. Pump.fun’s website continued operating during the suspension, but how long can any platform thrive when its primary marketing channel can vanish overnight? The takeaway is in black and white. In the crypto industry’s ongoing battle between innovation and regulation, social media platforms have become the new battleground. And as Pump.fun’s rollercoaster week shows, the rules of engagement are being written in real time, with billions of dollars hanging in the balance. title: JPMorgan Introduces USD Deposit Token on Coinbase’s Base Blockchain
body: U.S. banking giant JPMorgan has announced the pilot of a permissioned USD deposit token called JPMD on Base, the layer 2 Ethereum network built by listed exchange Coinbase (COIN). Earlier this week, the bank filed a trademark application for a crypto-focused platform named JPMD, designed to to offer services such as trading, exchange, transfer, and payment services for digital assets, as well as issuance of digital assets. The institution-focused JPMD, an alternative to stablecoins for the bank’s clients, marks the first deployment of JPMorgan’s Kinexys distributed ledger technology studio on a public blockchain, according to a press release. Banks and other enterprise players are crowding into the stablecoin space ahead of soon-to-land rules around dollar-pegged tokens in the U.S. JPMorgan garnered lots of attention for its so-called JPM Coin, a token for settling the cash leg of trades on its private blockchain, then called Onyx Digital Assets. “We are thrilled to see one of the world’s most prominent banks come onchain,” said Jesse Pollak, Creator of Base and VP of Engineering at Coinbase. “Base offers sub-second, sub-cent, 24/7 settlement, which makes fund transfers between J.P. Morgan institutional clients nearly instant. Coinbase is a proud J.P. Morgan institutional client, and this pilot combines the credibility of both J.P. Morgan and Base to help bring institutional money into a more global economy.”

title: Bank of America’s June survey shows global investors favor international stocks over U.S. assets for the next five years
body: International stocks have officially taken the lead in global investor strategy for the next half decade, with the United States falling behind. That’s straight from Bank of America’s latest June fund manager survey, which found that money managers are betting hard on foreign equities to deliver the best returns through 2030. The numbers are brutal for the US—less than 25% of those surveyed think American assets will lead the pack. Just 5% expect bonds to perform best. The rest are moving their cash outside the US borders. Bank of America strategist Michael Hartnett spelled it out in the report: “Less than [one quarter] think US assets will continue to dominate ranked returns.” Instead, investors are now crowding into emerging markets, Eurozone equities, and banks. The confidence in US stocks has dropped hard, and the reasons aren’t subtle. Investors move money out of the dollar and into gold, ACWX, and emerging markets So far in 2025, the numbers speak for themselves. The iShares MSCI All-Country World Index ex-US ETF (ACWX) is up 15% this year. The S&P 500? Just 2.6%. That puts ACWX at its highest outperformance versus the S&P 500 since the fund was created in 2008. The rotation out of the US isn’t a theory—it’s already happening. Meanwhile, confidence in the US dollar has collapsed. Investor positioning in the dollar has dropped to the lowest point in over 20 years. The big driver here is President Donald Trump’s aggressive trade stance. Earlier this year, the White House slapped steep tariffs on imports. Some of those were paused for 90 days during talks with major trade partners, but the threat hasn’t gone away. Uncertainty around trade has made investors question the dollar’s status as a safe place to park money. That vacuum has pulled capital into gold, now the top pick for the third straight month. Hartnett said that 41% of investors ranked gold as their most crowded trade. The long run of the Magnificent 7 tech stocks being the dominant bet is now over, with that trade falling to 23%. That “Magnificent 7” trade had held the top spot for two full years, but it’s officially been dethroned. The rest of the survey shows how bad the US outlook has become in investors’ eyes. In June, fund managers were most overweight in the Eurozone, EM, and banks, while the biggest underweights were US stocks, the US dollar, and energy. The reallocation is broad and sharp. It’s not about trimming exposure—it’s a clear message that the big money is going elsewhere. There’s also volatility playing into all this. Tensions in Europe and the Middle East are pushing even more capital into defensive trades like gold, but investors aren’t running from all risk—they’re just picking different bets. That’s why global equities, especially in developing markets, are seeing more inflows. Stocks in those regions are cheaper than the US, and right now, that’s more attractive than anything trading at a premium on Wall Street. One company caught in the middle of all this is Etsy. On Tuesday morning, Truist Securities bumped its price target on the company to $60, up from $55. That implies an 11% upside from Monday’s closing level. Analysts are telling investors to buy the dip, even though the company faces exposure from the De Minimis exemption being eliminated in China. Youssef Squali, an analyst at Truist, wrote: “While the company does have exposure to the De Minimis exemption being eliminated in China, we believe it’s relatively better insulated than some of its competitors including Temu (owned by PDD, [not rated]) and Shein (private), which have started raising prices on goods as a result of the Chinese tariffs, and the end of the De Minimis exemption.” Cryptopolitan Academy: Tired of market swings? title: Brazil Explores Bold Bitcoin Reserve Strategy
body: BitcoinWorld Brazil Explores Bold Bitcoin Reserve Strategy Exciting developments are unfolding in Latin America! Brazil is taking a significant step towards potentially integrating Bitcoin into its national financial strategy. A bill proposing the allocation of a portion of the country’s foreign exchange reserves to Bitcoin has successfully navigated its initial legislative hurdle. This move, if fully enacted, could position Brazil as a major player in the sovereign adoption of digital assets. What is the Brazil Bitcoin Reserve Bill (RESBiT)? The core of this legislative push is Bill 4501/2023, known as the RESBiT initiative. This proposal outlines a plan to allocate up to 5% of Brazil’s foreign exchange reserves into Bitcoin. Foreign exchange reserves are assets held by a central bank or monetary authority, usually in foreign currencies like the US dollar, Euro, or Yen, along with gold and other financial instruments. They serve crucial purposes such as stabilizing the national currency, managing liquidity, and providing confidence in the country’s financial stability. The idea behind RESBiT is to diversify these reserves by including Bitcoin. The bill has recently passed its first committee stage, a critical step in the long legislative process. This initial success signals growing interest and potential acceptance within Brazilian political circles regarding the strategic role of Bitcoin. Why Would Brazil Consider Bitcoin Reserves? Allocating national reserves to a volatile asset like Bitcoin is a bold move. Several potential motivations could be driving this initiative: Diversification: Reducing reliance on traditional reserve assets and currencies. Inflation Hedge: Viewing Bitcoin as a potential store of value against inflation, similar to gold. Innovation and Technology Adoption: Signaling Brazil’s embrace of digital assets and blockchain technology. Attracting Investment: Potentially making Brazil a more attractive destination for cryptocurrency businesses and investors. Strategic Positioning: Following the lead of other nations or positioning Brazil as a leader in the digital asset space. The proposal suggests a maximum allocation of 5%, indicating a cautious approach rather than a full pivot. This percentage allows for exposure to Bitcoin’s potential upside while limiting the overall risk to the nation’s critical foreign exchange reserves. How Does This Compare to El Salvador’s Bitcoin Strategy? If Bill 4501/2023 becomes law, Brazil would become the second Latin American nation to formally adopt a Bitcoin reserve strategy at the sovereign level, following El Salvador. However, the approaches differ significantly. El Salvador: Made Bitcoin legal tender, acquired significant Bitcoin holdings directly using state funds, and built infrastructure like the Chivo wallet. Their strategy is more integrated into the national economy and aims for broader adoption. Brazil: The RESBiT bill focuses specifically on allocating a portion of existing foreign exchange reserves. It does not propose making Bitcoin legal tender or integrating it directly into daily transactions for citizens on the same scale as El Salvador. It’s primarily a reserve management strategy. Brazil’s potential move is less about making Bitcoin a currency for its citizens and more about treating it as a strategic asset within its national treasury management. This distinction is crucial when evaluating the potential impact and goals of the RESBiT initiative. What Are the Potential Benefits and Challenges of Bitcoin Reserves? Adding Bitcoin to national reserves comes with potential rewards and significant risks. Potential Benefits: Exposure to a high-growth asset class. Potential hedge against global economic instability or currency devaluation. Increased financial sovereignty by holding an asset not tied to any single government or central bank. Setting a precedent for other nations, potentially increasing Bitcoin’s global legitimacy. Potential Challenges: Volatility: Bitcoin’s price is known for dramatic swings, which could impact the value of reserves. Security: Ensuring the secure storage of private keys for national Bitcoin holdings is paramount and complex. Regulatory Uncertainty: The global regulatory landscape for Bitcoin is still evolving. Public and Political Opposition: Skepticism about Bitcoin’s stability and utility could lead to significant internal debate. Liquidity: While Bitcoin is highly liquid, managing large national holdings during times of crisis could present unique challenges. The 5% allocation proposed in the RESBiT bill suggests an awareness of these challenges, aiming for a balance between potential upside and risk mitigation for Brazil’s financial stability. What Happens Next for the Bitcoin Bill in Brazil? Passing the first committee stage is a positive signal, but it is only one step in a multi-stage legislative journey in Brazil. Conclusion: Brazil’s Bold Step in the World of Bitcoin Reserves Brazil’s advancement of the RESBiT bill marks a significant moment in the global conversation around sovereign Bitcoin adoption. title: Coinbase Seeks SEC Approval to Offer Tokenized Stock Trading
body: Coinbase is seeking approval from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to launch tokenized stock trading, a move that could expand its business into the territory of traditional brokerage firms. The crypto exchange’s chief legal officer, Paul Grewal, told Reuters that Coinbase aims to offer digital versions of stocks — known as tokenized equities — which would trade on blockchain networks rather than through conventional exchanges. The model could allow round-the-clock trading, reduce transaction costs and eliminate clearing intermediaries. However, the road ahead depends on how the SEC responds. Coinbase is looking to secure either a no-action letter or an exemption from enforcement, both of which would provide regulatory cover for offering these products in the U.S. The push marks a strategic shift for Coinbase, which already owns a broker-dealer license through a dormant affiliate. If the initiative succeeds, it could position the company alongside retail brokerages like Robinhood (HOOD) and Charles Schwab (SCHW), which cater to a similar investor base, as well as crypto exchange Kraken . Tokenized equities aren’t yet legal to trade in the U.S., but platforms like Kraken are piloting such offerings overseas. Coinbase’s timing aligns with a friendlier regulatory climate under new SEC chair Paul Atkins; the agency has dropped several crypto-related lawsuits and set up a task force dedicated to digital assets. Still, Grewal declined to say whether Coinbase had formally filed its request. The confidence that comes from clear SEC guidance has been missing, he said. “Exciting? Yes. Important? Absolutely. But breaking news? Not exactly. We've been saying since earlier this year that the SEC should enable markets to unlock tokenized securities,” Grewal posted on social media. “Tokenized debt, equity, and investment funds present an opportunity for tailored regulation for securities that are offered and traded via digitally native methods.”

title: VanEck Warns of Emerging Risk for Bitcoin Treasury Companies, Outlines Strategies To Combat Capital Erosion
body: An analyst from one of the biggest asset managers in crypto is warning Bitcoin treasury companies that they need to pay attention to the ratio of their shares compared to their BTC net asset values (NAV). Matthew Sigel, the head of digital assets research at VanEck, says that no public BTC treasury companies have traded below their Bitcoin NAVs for a sustained period. However, Sigel notes that one company, the US medical tech firm Semler Scientific, is approaching parity. “As some of these companies raise capital through large at-the-market (ATM) programs to buy BTC, a risk is emerging: if the stock trades at or near NAV, continued equity issuance can dilute rather than create value. That is not capital formation. It is erosion. Companies pursuing a Bitcoin treasury strategy should adopt safeguards now, while premiums still exist. Some ideas: Announce pause to ATM issuance if the stock trades below 0.95 times NAV for 10 or more trading days. Prioritize buybacks when BTC appreciates, but the equity fails to reflect that value. Launch a strategic review if NAV discount persists. That might include a merger, spinoff, or sunset of the BTC strategy.” Sigel also argues that executive compensation should align with NAV per share growth, not with total share count or size of the Bitcoin position. “We’ve seen this movie before with the miners: persistent issuance and outsized executive pay. No need for a sequel. Once you are trading at NAV, shareholder dilution is no longer strategic. It is extractive. Boards and shareholders should act with discipline now, while they still have the benefit of optionality.” Last week, top pseudonymous trader DonAlt warned that he thinks Bitcoin treasury companies will be the source of massive selling pressure in the next bear market. “Bitcoin treasury companies… will be the reason for the next bear market being as violent as prior bear markets, and no one can convince me otherwise. title: ARK Invest Dumps $52M in Circle Shares—Signal or Strategy?
body: Cathie Wood’s ARK Invest has sold $52 million worth of Circle (CRCL) shares just 11 days after the stablecoin giant’s blockbuster IPO, sparking debate over whether the move signals broader concerns about Circle’s valuation or is simply a textbook portfolio rebalance after explosive gains. The Sale: Timing, Size, and Context ARK offloaded 342,658 Circle shares across three of its flagship ETFs—ARK Innovation (ARKK), Next Generation Internet (ARKW), and Fintech Innovation (ARKF)—on June 16, 2025. This marks ARK’s first sale of Circle stock since acquiring 4.49 million shares at IPO, a stake then valued at $373 million. Despite the sale, ARK still holds over 4.15 million shares worth roughly $628 million, maintaining Circle as a top holding in its funds. The timing is notable: Circle’s stock price has soared nearly 5x from its $31 IPO price to close at $151, with an intraday high of $165.60—an astonishing 387% surge in less than two weeks. ARK’s average purchase price was around $96, meaning the firm locked in a 50% gain on this tranche. Is This a Red Flag for Circle’s Valuation? Some market watchers see ARK’s move as a classic case of profit-taking after a parabolic rally, not an indictment of Circle’s long-term prospects. ARK has a history of trimming positions after sharp run-ups—recently doing the same with Coinbase and Robinhood—while maintaining core exposure to high-conviction names. On the day of the Circle sale, ARK also reduced Meta holdings and added to Nvidia and DoorDash, underscoring its dynamic approach to portfolio management. Equity analysts are split on Circle’s outlook. Bulls point to Circle’s massive USDC ecosystem, strong regulatory compliance, and a capital-light, high-margin business model. Bears, however, warn that Circle’s revenues are highly sensitive to interest rates, with 99% of Q1 2025 net income coming from interest on USDC reserves. If rates fall or stablecoin competition heats up, Circle’s earnings could face pressure. Comparing to Other ARK Fintech Exits ARK’s Circle sale fits a broader pattern: the firm frequently trims fintech winners after major rallies, as seen with Coinbase, Robinhood, and others in 2024–2025. These moves are typically framed as risk management rather than a loss of faith in the underlying business. Circle remains a top-3 holding in ARKW and ARKF, just behind Coinbase. On-Chain USDC Velocity: What’s the Data Say? On-chain data shows USDC’s velocity—how often the stablecoin changes hands—has climbed steadily in 2025, rising from 3.45e-12 to 5.50e-12 in Q1 alone. This uptick signals growing usage in DeFi, payments, and institutional settlements, supporting bullish arguments for Circle’s long-term growth. USDC’s expansion to new blockchains like XRP Ledger and World Chain further boosts its utility and network effects. Analyst Commentary: Q3 Outlook for Circle Looking ahead, equity analysts remain cautiously optimistic. Some see Circle’s stock as a potential $300 candidate if USDC circulation and platform revenues continue to scale. Others urge caution, citing the risk of post-IPO insider selling and the company’s reliance on interest income. The consensus: Circle’s Q3 earnings and USDC adoption trends will be critical in justifying its lofty valuation. The Bottom Line ARK Invest’s $52 million Circle sale is more a sign of disciplined portfolio management than a red flag for Circle’s future. With USDC adoption rising and Circle’s stock still a core ARK holding, all eyes now turn to Q3 earnings—and whether the stablecoin leader can maintain its momentum in a fast-evolving fintech landscape.

title: JPMorgan Chase Files To Launch Own Crypto Services Trademark Under ‘JPMD’
body: One of the world’s leading financial firms is filing a trademark to launch its new crypto services provider, JPMD. According to a new application with the United States Patent and Trademark Office, JPMorgan Chase Bank is seeking to trademark JPMD for a new cryptocurrency services platform. Walmart, Amazon, and other massive global companies are reportedly also looking into the benefits of having their own stablecoins. According to a report by The Wall Street Journal, anonymous people familiar with the matter say that some of the world’s largest retailers are considering issuing their very own dollar-pegged crypto assets in the US in an effort to save billions of dollars in transaction fees. Such a move would mark a major shift away from the traditional finance system, which includes the nation’s largest banks and credit providers. title: Bitcoin Strategy: Fold Secures Massive $250M Facility to Boost Corporate Bitcoin Holdings
body: BitcoinWorld Bitcoin Strategy: Fold Secures Massive $250M Facility to Boost Corporate Bitcoin Holdings In a significant move signaling strong confidence in the digital asset space, Fold Holdings, the company behind the popular Fold App that rewards users in Bitcoin, has announced a substantial financial maneuver designed to bolster its corporate balance sheet with more of the world’s leading cryptocurrency. This development underscores a growing trend among forward-thinking companies to integrate Bitcoin into their financial strategies. What Does This $250M Equity Facility Mean for Fold App? According to a press release via GlobeNewswire, Fold Holdings has entered into a $250 million equity purchase facility. This isn’t a direct cash injection upfront, but rather an agreement that allows Fold to sell up to $250 million worth of its equity (stock) to a specific investor over time, at Fold’s discretion. The key takeaway? Fold plans to use the vast majority of the proceeds generated from selling this equity primarily to acquire more Bitcoin for its corporate treasury . For users of the Fold App , which is known for offering Bitcoin rewards on everyday spending, this move signals a deepening commitment to the Bitcoin ecosystem. It positions Fold not just as a platform for earning Bitcoin, but as a company fundamentally aligned with Bitcoin’s long-term value proposition. Why Are Companies Building a Corporate Bitcoin Treasury? Fold isn’t the first company to strategically add Bitcoin to its balance sheet. MicroStrategy, led by Michael Saylor, pioneered this approach, accumulating billions of dollars worth of Bitcoin. Other companies have followed suit, albeit on a smaller scale. The primary reasons companies opt for a corporate Bitcoin strategy often include: Hedge Against Inflation: Bitcoin’s fixed supply is seen by many as a potential hedge against the devaluation of fiat currencies. Store of Value: Bitcoin is viewed as a digital gold, offering a durable store of value outside traditional financial systems. Growth Potential: Companies anticipate potential significant appreciation in Bitcoin’s value over time, boosting their balance sheet. Innovation and Signaling: Holding Bitcoin can signal a company’s forward-thinking approach and embrace of digital innovation. Fold’s decision to use a significant equity facility specifically for this purpose highlights the strategic importance they place on accumulating this digital asset. Understanding the Equity Facility Mechanism An equity purchase facility, also known as a committed equity facility or standby equity distribution agreement (SEDA), is a funding arrangement where a company (Fold) has the right, but not the obligation, to sell shares to an investor (the facility provider) over a set period and up to a maximum amount ($250 million). Here’s a simplified breakdown: Fold needs capital, in this case, to buy Bitcoin . They decide to draw down on the facility, selling a certain number of shares to the investor. The investor buys the shares, providing cash to Fold. Fold uses this cash to purchase Bitcoin for its corporate treasury . This process can be repeated until the $250 million limit is reached or the agreement expires. This method provides Fold with flexible access to capital, allowing them to raise funds when market conditions are favorable for selling equity and, subsequently, for buying Bitcoin . Analyzing Fold’s Specific Bitcoin Strategy Fold’s Bitcoin strategy appears multifaceted. Firstly, it’s about strengthening the company’s balance sheet with what they believe is a appreciating asset. This aligns with the broader corporate Bitcoin trend. Secondly, it could be seen as a strategic alignment with their core business. A company focused on rewarding users in Bitcoin naturally enhances its brand and mission by holding a significant amount of Bitcoin itself. It builds trust and demonstrates a long-term belief in the asset they promote. Thirdly, utilizing an equity facility offers flexibility. Fold can time their equity sales and subsequent Bitcoin purchases based on market conditions, potentially allowing them to acquire Bitcoin at opportune moments. Placing Fold’s Move in the Context of Institutional Bitcoin Adoption Fold’s significant funding round specifically aimed at increasing its Institutional Bitcoin holdings is a strong indicator of the continued maturation and adoption of Bitcoin by corporate entities. While not as large as MicroStrategy’s holdings, a $250 million facility dedicated primarily to Bitcoin acquisition is a substantial commitment for a company like Fold. This move contributes to the overall narrative of Institutional Bitcoin adoption, showing that it’s not just large, publicly traded companies considering this asset class, but also growth-stage companies within the crypto ecosystem itself. Key Considerations: Benefits and Challenges Like any strategic financial decision, building a Crypto Treasury with a volatile asset like Bitcoin comes with potential benefits and challenges: Benefits: Enhanced Balance Sheet: Potential for significant asset appreciation if Bitcoin’s value increases. Strategic Alignment: Reinforces Fold’s brand identity as a Bitcoin-centric company. Inflation Hedge: Provides potential protection against the declining purchasing power of fiat currency. Flexibility: The equity facility allows for opportunistic funding and purchasing. Challenges: Price Volatility: Bitcoin’s price can fluctuate dramatically, potentially leading to significant paper losses on the balance sheet. Market Timing Risk: Deciding when to draw on the facility and when to buy Bitcoin involves market timing risk. Execution Risk: Successfully executing the equity facility agreement requires navigating financial markets. Regulatory Uncertainty: The regulatory landscape for corporate crypto holdings is still evolving. Actionable Insights for the Reader What can we learn from Fold’s strategic move? Corporate Confidence: This action signals continued confidence in Bitcoin’s long-term value proposition among companies operating within the space. Alternative Funding: It demonstrates how companies are using innovative financial structures like equity facilities to fund strategic asset acquisitions. Alignment Matters: For companies whose business is tied to Bitcoin, holding Bitcoin on their balance sheet reinforces their commitment and vision. Risk is Present: While the potential upside is clear, the inherent volatility of Bitcoin means this strategy is not without risk. Conclusion: A Bold Step for Fold’s Bitcoin Strategy Fold’s securing of a $250 million equity facility with the primary goal of acquiring more Bitcoin for its corporate treasury is a powerful statement. It reflects a calculated Bitcoin strategy aimed at leveraging the potential growth of the digital asset while reinforcing the company’s identity within the ecosystem. This move adds another notable example to the growing list of companies embracing Institutional Bitcoin adoption, further solidifying Bitcoin’s position as a legitimate asset class for corporate balance sheets. As the Fold App continues to grow its user base, its own financial health, potentially boosted by a strong Crypto Treasury , could become an increasingly important factor. title: Elon’s xAI is burning over $1 billion every month and plans to spend $13 billion in 2025
body: Elon’s AI startup xAI is torching through money at a speed that would bankrupt most companies in months. The company is trying to raise $9.3 billion in a mix of debt and equity, but even before locking that down, more than half of it is already earmarked to be spent in just three months, based on deal terms shown to investors. That cash drain is tied to the company’s $13 billion projected burn rate for 2025—over $1 billion every month, without pause, according to Bloomberg. Elon’s company is behind the AI chatbot Grok, and despite all the buzz, it expects to make just $500 million in revenue this year. Meanwhile, OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT, expects to rake in $12.7 billion in the same period. Meanwhile amid this, the NAACP and the Southern Environmental Law Center said Tuesday they plan to sue Elon’s xAI over air pollution from its Memphis data center. The site runs on gas turbines and began operating last year without a permit. Attorney Patrick Anderson said there’s no legal exemption for the turbines and the facility has been active for over 364 days, which violates state rules. xAI claims it’s following the law and says its “temporary power units are operating in compliance with all applicable laws.” xAI struggles to match rivals while cash keeps vanishing Despite being backed by the world’s richest man, xAI is still fighting for air in an industry where hardware, not hype, decides who wins. The cost of building out AI infrastructure—which includes custom server farms and rare high-powered chips—is punishing. Harvey Schwartz, CEO of Carlyle Group, told shareholders that AI buildout globally will require $1.8 trillion by the end of the decade. All this has left startups like xAI burning through investor cash at a breakneck speed. That battle is costing xAI more than it’s making. The company has been bleeding cash trying to catch up with better-funded and more established competitors like Anthropic and OpenAI, both of which have clearer monetization paths. Source: Bloomberg Elon’s team believes it has an edge, though, because it isn’t renting servers and chips like some competitors—it’s buying the infrastructure outright. That access comes from xAI’s ties to X, Elon’s social media company formerly known as Twitter. X bought up a large stash of specialized AI chips, and xAI now has direct access to them. Elon has also told investors that xAI plans to keep buying more chips. xAI leans on social media data and investor hype to stay afloat After merging with X, xAI is using the platform’s massive, constantly updating archive of user content to train its models. That lets them dodge the costs that come with paying for licensed datasets like others in the space. This setup is what has Elon’s team claiming xAI will be profitable by 2027. OpenAI, by comparison, expects cash flow positivity in 2029, per Bloomberg’s earlier report. That projection, mixed with Elon’s name recognition and political clout, has kept investors interested—at least for now. Before tensions recently rose between Elon and President Donald Trump, the company’s value was climbing. xAI’s valuation hit $80 billion at the end of the first quarter of 2025, up from $51 billion at the end of 2024. Notable investors include Andreessen Horowitz, Sequoia Capital, and VY Capital. But fundraising hasn’t come easily. Since its founding in 2023, xAI has raised $14 billion in equity. By the start of this year, just $4 billion of that was left. Internal forecasts expected almost all of it to be gone by the end of Q2. To stay ahead of the burn, xAI is now finalizing a new $4.3 billion equity round, and it’s already told investors it plans to raise another $6.4 billion in 2026. That’s not even counting the $5 billion in corporate debt that Morgan Stanley is helping xAI rais e. That debt is supposed to fund data center development. Unlike some competitors that choose to fund each project separately, Elon’s company is choosing to go big all at once. To ease the burn slightly, the company told investors it expects a $650 million rebate from one of its chip manufacturers. That won’t solve the problem but might buy them a bit more time. The original pitch didn’t go over well with some investors. Bloomberg said there were early signs of resistance to the deal’s terms. In response, xAI gave a few select investors a deeper look at its financials earlier this week. That helped. Interest improved after the company adjusted the terms to be more investor-friendly and closed the equity raise. title: Coinbase Seeks SEC Approval to Launch Tokenized Stock Trading in US
body: Coinbase is asking the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for permission to offer tokenized stocks to its users. This move would put the leading crypto exchange in direct competition with major trading platforms like Robinhood and Charles Schwab. This would allow Coinbase to provide stock trading through blockchain technology, expanding its service beyond crypto. How Tokenized Stocks Could Transform Market Trading Tokenized equities are digital versions of company shares that exist on a blockchain. Instead of owning the actual stock, investors hold a digital token representing it. These tokens can be traded on blockchain platforms like Bitcoin (BTC). Supporters say tokenized stocks could lower costs by cutting out middlemen, making trades faster, and allowing trading outside regular market hours. In 2024, industry leaders predicted that the Real-world asset (RWA) tokenization could reach over $600 billion in assets under management (AUM) by 2030. However, a recent World Economic Forum report said tokenized stocks often lack enough buyers and sellers, making trading harder. There are also no clear global rules yet, which could slow their adoption. In May, Robinhood proposed a federal framework to the SEC to help support tokenizing real-world assets. The goal is to modernize U.S. markets and make them more efficient and accessible. Coinbase Seeks SEC Approval to Trade Tokenized Stocks Trading tokenized stocks is currently not allowed in the U.S. For Coinbase to move ahead, it needs special approval from the SEC, which is called a “no-action letter.” This means the agency will not take legal action if the company offers the service. Coinbase is not registered as a broker-dealer, which is usually required to trade securities. In 2023, the SEC sued the exchange for acting like one without permission. However, the case was later dropped during President Trump’s administration. Coinbase’s top lawyer, Paul Grewal, recently said this is a significant priority. He did not confirm if the trading platform has officially asked the SEC yet, but said a no-action letter would give companies more confidence to move forward. Trump Administration Takes Softer Stance on Crypto Coinbase’s move comes as the U.S. government shifts to a more crypto-friendly approach. President Trump has supported the industry by meeting with crypto leaders at the White House and nominating pro-crypto regulators. This regulatory change has boosted confidence in the market. As a result, Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies have hit new highs this year as more investors get involved. Under Trump, the SEC has also dropped lawsuits against big crypto firms like Coinbase, Binance, and Kraken. A new task force is now working on more explicit rules for digital assets, marking a fresh start for the industry. title: JPMorgan Chase has officially revealed plans to launch its JPMD tokens on Base
body: JPMorgan Chase announced it would launch its native JPMD token on the Base network. The news come just a day after JP Morgan filed a trademark for the JPMD ticker. JPMorgan Chase made another step toward crypto integration by announcing it would issue its own JPMD token on the Base network. JPMD will represent dollar deposits in the world’s biggest bank, bridging another gap between fiat and crypto. The pilot JPMD token will also be launched on Coinbase for early tests. The first transaction is expected to happen within days. JPMorgan has already minted tokens in a digital wallet and will deposit them to the crypto exchange, using the Base L2 chain. While Base is open to anyone, the JPMD token will be restricted only to the whitelisted clients of JPMorgan. For JPMorgan, the new token is the first foray into a crypto ecosystem outside its internal distributed ledger testing. The bank already runs an exclusive access chain, Kinexys Digital Payments, formerly JPM Coin, which allows the bank’s clients to move their funds in the form of tokens. JPMD will be available for institutional clients The JPMD asset will be denominated in US dollars and represent deposits in the bank. The asset will be used in a pilot program running for several months and will be available to Coinbase’s institutional clients. The token will not be freely used among users and retail clients. JP Morgan has also hinted at other currencies, launching additional specialized stablecoins pending regulator approval. The bank will launch its stablecoin as acceptance of digital dollar-denominated assets is growing. The launch arrives just a week after the Genius Bill on stablecoins passed a key vote and headed to the US Senate. Deposit tokens are not totally similar to stablecoins, as they represent a deposit claim against a commercial bank. They are a digital version of the deposits belonging to customers, hence fully backed by fiat. The JPMD asset will be the first instance of tokenizing direct bank deposits on a public blockchain, in this case, the widely used Base. “ From an institutional standpoint, deposit tokens are a superior alternative to stablecoins,” said Naveen Mallela, global co-head of the bank’s blockchain division. Unlike stablecoins, the deposit tokens can also bear the same interest as the deposit. The bank’s idea is that the JPMD asset will target users who are looking for an alternative to stablecoins produced by a commercial bank. Currently, stablecoins may have trouble securing banking services and showing proof of deposits, which would be trivial for JPMorgan. JP Morgan manages roughly $10T transactions daily, of which $2B go through its native chain. Adopting Base will give the bank another access to a public network with minimal costs and a chance to connect to the wider Ethereum ecosystem, as well as Coinbase’s institutional user base. The bank will continue to grow its Kinexys network, with a different user base. The bank has tested multiple on-chain payment techniques and believes deposit tokens may become a widely used form of money for the digital ecosystem. Currently, transferring fiat into stablecoins is not always smooth for either retail or institutional investors, with each stablecoin having different requirements. With deposit tokens, the bank’s clients may easily find their balance on Coinbase. KEY Difference Wire : the secret tool crypto projects use to get guaranteed media coverage

title: Ondo Finance Accelerates Tokenized Securities Future with Global Alliance
body: BitcoinWorld Ondo Finance Accelerates Tokenized Securities Future with Global Alliance The world of finance is undergoing a rapid transformation, driven by the potential of blockchain technology. A significant step forward has just been announced by Ondo Finance , a key player in bringing real-world assets onto the blockchain. They have formed the Global Markets Alliance , a powerful coalition aimed at tackling one of the biggest hurdles to mainstream adoption: standardization in the realm of tokenized securities . Why is Standardization Crucial for Tokenized Securities? Imagine trying to use different types of currency that couldn’t be exchanged, or trying to connect devices that use incompatible plugs. That’s a simplified view of the challenge facing digital assets today, particularly tokenized securities . While the concept of representing ownership of real-world assets like stocks, bonds, or real estate on a blockchain is incredibly promising, the lack of unified standards creates significant friction. Here’s why standardization is paramount: Interoperability: Without common standards, different platforms, wallets, and protocols cannot easily interact. This makes it difficult to move tokenized securities between different blockchains or trading venues. Liquidity: Fragmentation hinders liquidity. If assets are siloed on specific platforms due to compatibility issues, it’s harder for buyers and sellers to find each other, leading to wider spreads and less efficient markets. Investor Protection: Clear, agreed-upon standards can help define asset characteristics, ownership rights, and transfer rules, offering better clarity and protection for investors. Regulatory Clarity: Standard practices can provide regulators with a clearer framework to understand and potentially supervise the market for tokenized securities . Ease of Adoption: Standard interfaces and processes make it easier for traditional financial institutions and individual investors to engage with digital assets without needing bespoke solutions for every interaction. Introducing the Global Markets Alliance Recognizing these challenges, Ondo Finance has taken a proactive step by initiating the Global Markets Alliance . Announced via their official blog, this coalition brings together a diverse group of prominent entities from the blockchain and digital asset space. The stated goal is clear: to collaboratively establish shared standards for the issuance, management, and trading of tokenized securities . The initial members represent various crucial layers of the digital asset ecosystem: Blockchain Infrastructure: Solana Foundation (representing a major blockchain network) Wallet Providers: Bitget Wallet, Trust Wallet, Rainbow Wallet (critical for users to hold and interact with assets) DeFi Protocols: Jupiter, 1inch (important for trading and liquidity) Custodians & Infrastructure: BitGo, Fireblocks (essential for institutional adoption and secure asset handling) Trading Platforms/Brokers: Alpaca (bridging traditional and digital trading) Issuer/Protocol: Ondo Finance (pioneering RWA tokenization) This mix of participants is key. It ensures that the standards developed consider the needs of different stakeholders, from the underlying blockchain layer to the end-user’s wallet and the institutional infrastructure required for broad market participation. What Benefits Can the Global Markets Alliance Bring? The formation of this alliance signals a collective effort to unlock the full potential of tokenized securities . The anticipated benefits are substantial and could significantly accelerate the growth of the digital assets market. Key advantages include: Enhanced Interoperability: By agreeing on common token standards (like variations of ERC-20 or new, purpose-built standards), assets could move more freely across different platforms and potentially different blockchains via bridges. Increased Liquidity: Greater interoperability naturally leads to pooled liquidity. Assets wouldn’t be confined to a single platform, making them easier to buy and sell, thus improving market efficiency. Streamlined Development: Developers building applications or services around tokenized securities would have clear guidelines, reducing complexity and speeding up innovation. Improved Investor Confidence: Standardized practices regarding asset representation, transfer restrictions (like know-your-customer requirements), and legal frameworks can build trust among potential investors, both retail and institutional. Reduced Costs: Interoperable systems can lower the operational costs associated with managing and transferring securities compared to legacy systems. Think of it as building the foundational plumbing for a new financial system. Without agreed-upon pipe sizes and connections, every building would need a custom solution, which is inefficient and expensive. The alliance aims to provide that standardized plumbing. Challenges on the Path to Universal Blockchain Standards While the formation of the Global Markets Alliance is a positive development, the path to establishing widely adopted blockchain standards for tokenized securities is not without its hurdles. This is a complex undertaking involving multiple parties with potentially differing technical approaches and business interests. Potential challenges include: Achieving Consensus: Getting a diverse group of companies, some of whom might be competitors, to agree on specific technical standards and governance models can be difficult and time-consuming. Regulatory Uncertainty: The regulatory landscape for digital assets and tokenized securities is still evolving globally. Standards need to be flexible enough to adapt to different jurisdictional requirements. Integration with Legacy Systems: For widespread adoption, new standards must find ways to interface with existing traditional financial infrastructure, which is a significant technical challenge. Security Considerations: Standards must incorporate robust security measures to protect against hacks, fraud, and operational risks inherent in digital systems. Adoption Inertia: Even with established standards, convincing the broader market – including traditional financial institutions and other blockchain projects – to adopt them requires significant effort and time. The alliance will need strong leadership and a clear roadmap to navigate these complexities effectively. Their success will depend on their ability to find common ground and demonstrate the practical benefits of their proposed standards. What Does This Alliance Mean for the Future of Digital Assets? The initiative by Ondo Finance and its partners is a significant indicator of the maturing digital assets market. It shows a move beyond simply tokenizing assets towards building the necessary infrastructure for a functional, scalable, and widely accessible market for tokenized securities . If successful, the Global Markets Alliance could: Accelerate Institutional Adoption: Standardized, predictable frameworks are crucial for traditional financial institutions to confidently enter the space. Drive Innovation: Clear standards provide a stable base upon which developers can build new financial products and services leveraging tokenized securities . Improve Market Efficiency: Enhanced interoperability and liquidity will make the trading and management of digital assets more efficient. Expand Use Cases: As standards become established, we may see a broader range of assets being tokenized, from private equity and debt to unique collectibles and intellectual property. This collaborative approach, bringing together different parts of the ecosystem, is essential. No single company can establish universal blockchain standards alone. Alliances like this are vital for fostering industry-wide cooperation. Actionable Insights for the Community For investors, developers, and market participants interested in the future of digital assets and tokenized securities , the formation of the Global Markets Alliance is something to watch closely. Stay Informed: Follow the progress of the alliance and the standards they propose. Understanding the technical and operational standards will be key. Evaluate Platforms: As standards emerge, consider which platforms and protocols are adopting them, as this may indicate future interoperability and liquidity benefits. Understand the Risks: While standards aim to improve security and clarity, the market for tokenized securities is still nascent and carries risks related to technology, regulation, and market volatility. Explore Use Cases: Look into the various types of assets being tokenized by members like Ondo Finance to understand the practical applications of these developing standards. The move towards standardization is a long-term play, but one that is necessary for the digital asset market to reach its full potential and integrate with global finance. Conclusion: A Unified Vision for Digital Assets The announcement of the Global Markets Alliance by Ondo Finance and its esteemed members marks a pivotal moment in the evolution of tokenized securities and the broader digital assets landscape. By committing to the creation of shared blockchain standards , this coalition is directly addressing the fragmentation that has hindered mainstream adoption. The collaborative effort to enhance interoperability, liquidity, and investor protections lays the groundwork for a more robust, efficient, and accessible market for real-world assets on the blockchain. While challenges remain, the unified vision demonstrated by this alliance offers a compelling glimpse into a future where tokenized securities play a central role in global finance, powered by open and agreed-upon standards. title: Polygon’s zkEVM Never Adopted Blobs, Now Running at a $1M+ Annual Loss: Researcher Claims
body: Polygon’s zero-knowledge chain, zkEVM, which was originally acquired through the $250 million purchase of Hermez in 2021, appears to have fallen flat. According to GrowThePie’s research lead, Lorenz Lehmann, Polygon zkEVM has seen little meaningful progress since its rebranding and is now operating at an annual loss of over $1 million. “Development Quietly Abandoned” Lehmann claims development on the chain has been “quietly discontinued” and that it was never upgraded to incorporate Ethereum’s Blob data structure, which drastically reduces data availability costs for rollups. His comments arrive amid broader changes at the Polygon Foundation, where co-founder Sandeep Nailwal has recently stepped into the role of CEO. The leadership transition follows the quiet exit of co-founder Mihailo Bjelic, leaving Nailwal as the only founding member still actively involved. Two other co-founders, Jaynti Kanani and Anurag Arjun, exited operational roles in 2022. With this shift, Nailwal is now overseeing structural changes aimed at consolidating Polygon’s focus. While official communication has set 2026 as the target date to sunset zkEVM, Lehmann’s latest claim suggests that the shutdown process is already well underway behind the scenes. His remarks imply the decision to wind down zkEVM predates any formal announcement, and that Polygon’s current narrative may understate the degree to which the product has been deprioritized. Polygon zkEVM was once positioned as a major milestone of the project’s commitment to zero-knowledge scaling. But with continued losses, stagnating development, and a shift in focus toward its proof-of-stake chain and new initiatives like AggLayer, the chain’s role has been effectively marginalized. TVL Down By 80% Polygon zkEVM’s total value locked (TVL) reached an all-time high of $187 million in March 2024, according to data from L2Beat. Although it briefly rebounded to $111 million later that year, the overall trend has been downward. In 2025, the decline has accelerated, as the TVL dropped nearly 80%, from $80.2 million to just $16.25 million at the time of writing. title: X Purges Pump.fun and Memecoin Accounts Overnight
body: In a move that sent shockwaves through the crypto world, X (formerly Twitter) abruptly suspended the accounts of Pump.fun—the Solana-based memecoin launchpad—and its founder Alon Cohen, along with dozens of other high-profile memecoin and trading tool accounts. The crackdown, which began late on June 16, instantly cut off a vital communication channel for one of the most active and controversial corners of the crypto ecosystem, leaving traders, developers, and influencers scrambling for answers and alternatives. A Policy Shift—But No Clear Reason X has yet to provide an official explanation for the suspensions, displaying only its standard “violates the X Rules” message on affected profiles. Industry speculation is rampant. Some users point to the use of unauthorized third-party APIs as a likely trigger, with several banned platforms allegedly using unofficial tools to access X data and skirt the platform’s steep API fees. Others suspect the crackdown is related to mounting regulatory scrutiny, with rumors swirling of ongoing SEC investigations into Pump.fun’s rapid-fire launches and potential securities violations. The platform has faced lawsuits over allegedly unregistered securities and controversial tokens, and its high-profile, sometimes chaotic livestreams have previously drawn negative attention. Market Impact: Token Launches and Capital Flight The immediate fallout was dramatic. Within an hour of the suspensions, blockchain analytics showed a surge of new memecoins minted in reference to the bans, with five of these tokens breaking into the top 10 trending on DEX Screener and collectively driving over $10 million in volume. Meanwhile, 15 out of 31 tokens that “graduated” from Pump.fun’s bonding curve in the hour after the ban were directly linked to the incident, representing nearly 9% of all memecoins that completed the process that day. The removal of Pump.fun’s X account and those of other trading tool providers like GMGN, BullX, and Bloom Trading disrupted the flow of information and coordination for new token launches. Founders and traders, suddenly cut off from their main audience, reported sharp drops in engagement and liquidity. Real-time dashboards showed capital flowing out of affected tokens, with some traders fleeing to rival launchpads or even experimenting with decentralized social platforms to regroup. Community Response The memecoin community’s reaction was swift and chaotic. Within minutes, users began minting protest tokens and sharing screenshots of their favorite accounts’ suspensions. Telegram and Discord groups saw a spike in activity as traders and influencers sought new channels for updates and coordination. Some, like the GMGN team, announced they were appealing the bans and working with X to restore access, but many remain in limbo. The crackdown has also reignited debate over the role of centralized social media in crypto. With X’s unpredictable enforcement and lack of transparency, some memecoin founders and community leaders are now openly discussing a migration to decentralized social networks—platforms where account bans are impossible and community governance is the norm. Whether this shift gains traction remains to be seen, but the incident has highlighted just how vulnerable crypto communities are to sudden policy changes by major tech platforms. What’s Next for Memecoin Markets? As Pump.fun’s website and other affected platforms remain operational, the memecoin sector faces a period of heightened uncertainty. Upcoming token launches are likely to see reduced hype and liquidity, and the absence of major influencers and trading bots could reshape how new projects gain traction. At the same time, the crackdown may force the community to innovate—either by finding new ways to coordinate or by embracing decentralized alternatives for both trading and social interaction.
